[THOUGHT] A linear trio of intensely itchy papules ("breakfast–lunch–dinner" pattern) on exposed skin strongly suggests bedbug bites. Key missing exposure history is recent sleeping in unfamiliar lodging or new mattress where bedbugs are encountered. Asking about recent overnight stays will help confirm exposure without duplicating earlier questions.

[QUERY] Have you recently stayed overnight in a hotel, hostel, or other unfamiliar sleeping place (or had a new mattress/bedding) in the past week?

[REFERENCE] 8. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami.

[RESPONSE] Yes — I recently attended a business conference in Miami.

[THOUGHT] The presentation—intense pruritus, excoriated red papules arranged linearly as a cluster of three on the medial thigh, plus recent overnight hotel/conference stay—matches the classic "breakfast–lunch–dinner" pattern of bedbug (Cimex) bites. Alternative diagnoses (herpes zoster, contact dermatitis, fleas, mosquitoes) are less likely given absence of pain/vesicles, the localized linear cluster, and typical exposure history.

[DIAGNOSIS] Bedbug bites (Cimex lectularius)
